memory_update.text: ICHR and UCTT are the cleanest US-listed underfollowed candidates for semiconductor OEM tool subsystems: both map directly to gas/chemical/fluid delivery, outsourced subsystem manufacturing, cleanroom assembly, and qualification-dependent OEM relationships.

MKSI and AEIS should remain in the node universe as reference specialists, not primary underfollowed alpha names, because their subsystem exposure is direct but their market caps and awareness are higher than the preferred discovery range.

The semicap subsystem node splits into at least four investigable chokepoint subnodes: RF/plasma power delivery, vacuum/process control, high-purity gas/chemical delivery, and outsourced subsystem cleaning/assembly/analytics.

Next layer should verify OEM qualification lock-in with primary filings: customer concentration, named OEM customers, sole-source language, design-win persistence, cleanroom/capacity expansion, and product-specific content growth per tool.

node: Semiconductor equipment subsystems embedded inside OEM fab tools
summary: Layer 1B expansion found a focused US-listed universe around hidden semiconductor equipment subsystem suppliers. The best-fit underfollowed lane is fluid/gas/chemical delivery and outsourced subsystem manufacturing for OEM fab tools, led by ICHR and UCTT. MKSI and AEIS are included as larger reference specialists because their exposure to vacuum, RF/plasma power, process control, specialty chemistry, and measurement is unusually direct to the node. No buy/sell view is implied; this is a research funnel candidate set requiring later verification of customer concentration, OEM qualification durability, semiconductor capex sensitivity, margin cyclicality, and content-per-tool growth.
